summary.text: Yolanda Prince is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 1st District and a university project manager who won the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff over Dax Alexander.
Her BallotReady profile lists support for raising the minimum wage, teacher pay and a Medicare for All system.

paragraphs.text: Prince earned a bachelor's degree in public administration and public relations from Stephen F. Austin State University in 1998 and a master's degree in public administration from the University of Texas at Arlington in 2011, according to her BallotReady profile.
KETK reported that she has worked in education, nonprofit organizations and government.
Since 2022 she has worked as a project manager at Prairie View A&M University, and since 2005 she has been CEO of Datwoman, Inc., according to her BallotReady profile.

Prince has served as a precinct chair, election judge and president of the Democratic Club of Smith County for about a decade, and she was a delegate to the 2012 Democratic National Convention, KETK reported.

She finished first in the March 3, 2026 four-candidate Democratic primary and advanced to a runoff with Alexander; local coverage said her campaign focused on education, civil and voting rights, and healthcare.
Prince won the May 26, 2026 runoff, about 72 percent to 28 percent in reporting at the time, and became the party's nominee against Rep. Nathaniel Moran.
